description: The WIDTH a derived column declares: a CAST names a real parameterized type in every family (bare casts stay the family maximum, temporal parameters report as fractional-second scale, nesting takes the OUTER width narrowing included), a binary-returning function is as wide as its result (hashes their digest with SHA2 pinned at 64 whatever digest size, decoders a per-encoding ratio of the ARGUMENT's declared width), and a set operation is as wide as its WIDEST branch whichever leads - keeping the fixed BINARY spelling only when nothing widened it. Converted 1:1 from expressions/DerivedWidthTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE dw (s4 VARCHAR(4), s100 VARCHAR(100), s VARCHAR, b4 BINARY(4), b100 BINARY(100), t TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(s AS VARCHAR(10)) AS c FROM dw
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(s AS CHAR(7)) AS c FROM dw
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT s::VARCHAR(6) AS c FROM dw
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(b4 AS BINARY(10)) AS c FROM dw
CREATE TABLE dw (s4 VARCHAR(4), s100 VARCHAR(100), s VARCHAR, b4 BINARY(4), b100 BINARY(100), t TIMESTAMP_NTZ, n NUMBER)
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(t AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ(3)) AS c FROM dw
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(t AS TIMESTAMP_LTZ(6)) AS c FROM dw
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW dw_v AS SELECT CAST(t AS TIMESTAMP_NTZ) AS c FROM dw
